summary: Implemented, locally only (HD-0017), the minimum offline infrastructure for the first developer-to-reviewer experiment. A review packet builder and verifier (ops/review-packet.mjs, ops/lib/review-packet.mjs, ops/lib/review-text.mjs) binds a fixed set of files by SHA-256 to one commit, task and attempt; the reviewer instructions, task, policy, decision schema and requirements come from a trusted baseline commit and are checked byte for byte against the checkout the tool runs from; CI is recomputed from GitHub's fields; the worker's report and the diff text are labelled claims and instruction-like text is counted as data. A deterministic decision gate (ops/decision-gate.mjs, ops/lib/decision-gate.mjs) reuses the existing decision validator and returns REVIEW_VALID_HUMAN_APPROVAL_REQUIRED, REQUIRES_CORRECTIONS, REVIEW_REJECTED or REVIEW_INVALID; it always reports that a human is required and fixes merge, deploy, authorize and launch to false. One new schema and one new runtime value (manual_session) were added; policy 0.5.0, no rule relaxed. 48 new tests (suite 465 of 465), 6 of them on the real data of GitHub run 44082419253; a 63-weakening mutation check (62 caught, 1 equivalent). A runbook and the exact launch message for the first manual reviewer session were written; no reviewer was run. Project memory records the live OPS-0003 run (HD-0016), this task (HD-0017), OQ-0037 and ADR-0013, and corrects the statements that OPS-0003 had never run on GitHub. Nothing was pushed, merged, deployed or activated.

unresolved_issues.description: No reviewer has been run. The packet, the gate and the runbook were tested with mock decisions only, so nothing yet shows that a real separate Claude session produces a decision that binds to a packet and is useful.

The gate compares recorded session identifiers only; a reviewer can report any identifier. Session separation is not enforced by anything, and the repository still lacks enforced separation between the human owner and the identity Claude acts under (OQ-0036).

The packet builder and the gate are only as trustworthy as the baseline checkout they run from, and the trusted-base check remains advisory (OQ-0035). The first experiment's baseline is the owner-reviewed OPS-0004 commit, which depends on the owner's review of this task.
The gate does not understand prose: a persuasive but wrong review passes; instruction-like text detection is a short pattern list; the judge-owned path list is fixed. A human decides everything.
Getting the baseline commit onto the machine that runs the reviewer needs either a one-time push of this branch or a git bundle, an owner decision (OQ-0037). Nothing was pushed.
The eight Reel commits and the creative file-mode change are untouched. Their path set is disjoint from this branch's.

assumptions: started_at is the creation time of the task branch (from the reflog).

The packet for the real OPS-0003 change is rebuilt from the baseline and the stored real evidence file rather than committed, because committing it would change the baseline it records; its manifest hash is recorded in this report.

The real GitHub responses are stored unmodified and contain the owner's public account name and the commit-message attribution trailer; no email address of a person and no credential is in any committed file (checked by the validator's content scan).
Claude Code flags in the runbook were confirmed with `claude --help` for version 2.1.326 in this environment; a different version may differ.
questions_for_human: OQ-0037: how should the baseline commit reach the machine that runs the first reviewer session: a one-time push of claude/ops-0004-review-foundation (named in the approval), or a git bundle?
Do you accept the reviewed OPS-0004 commit as the trusted baseline for the first experiment (HD-0017)?
OQ-0035 and OQ-0036 remain open: which anchor for the trusted-base check, and whether a separate GitHub identity for Claude can be used.
